objects.title: A hiding place that gives you away
objects.literal_meaning: Are you hiding? Your two feet are showing!
objects.explanation: Someone’s attempt to conceal a matter leaves an obvious clue. The question punctures the pretence of secrecy: what is meant to be hidden is still visible. It can tease a transparent excuse without proving any particular accusation.
objects.meaning_odia: ଲୁଚିବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଚାଲିଛି, ହେଲେ ପାଦ ଦିଶୁଥିବାରୁ ଲୁଚା କଥାର ଆଭାସ ମିଳୁଛି। ନିଜେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଇଥିବା ଚିହ୍ନରୁ ଗୋପନ କଥା ପଦାରେ ପଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଏହା ବୁଝାଏ। ଲୁଚାଇବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଥିବା ଲୋକର ନିଜ ଅସାବଧାନତା ହିଁ ଏଠାରେ ହାସ୍ୟର କାରଣ।
objects.usage_example: A friend tries to keep a surprise parcel hidden, but its wrapping sticks out of the bag. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

objects.title: A noise that does not impress
objects.odia: କଂସାରୀ ଘର ପାରାଙ୍କୁ କୁଲା ଢାଉଁ ଢାଉଁ
objects.literal_meaning: To the bell-metal worker’s household pigeons: bang, bang with a winnowing tray!
objects.explanation: An attempt to startle or impress has little effect on someone already accustomed to the disturbance. The joke contrasts the small display of noise with the noisy workshop imagined around the birds. It can describe an empty threat made to an experienced listener.
objects.meaning_odia: ବଡ଼ ଶବ୍ଦ ଶୁଣି ଅଭ୍ୟସ୍ତ ପାରାକୁ ଛୋଟ ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଡରାଇବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟାରେ ହାସ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ଯିଏ ଆଗରୁ କଠିନ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଦେଖିଛନ୍ତି, ତାଙ୍କ ଆଗରେ ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଧମକ କାମ ନକରିପାରେ। ଏହା ଅନୁଭବର ତୁଳନା, କଂସାରି ବା ଅନ୍ୟ କୌଣସି ସମୁଦାୟର ଜନ୍ମଗତ ଗୁଣର ଦାବି ନୁହେଁ।
objects.usage_example: A seasoned performer remains calm when someone tries to unsettle them with a little backstage commotion. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
objects.cultural_context: The workshop and winnowing tray form the saying’s acoustic image. Kansari is translated through the craft role in this expression; it does not establish the identity of any present maker or an inherited community trait.

objects.title: A secret concealed inside an ordinary action
objects.odia: ବୁଡ଼ି କରି ପାଣି ପିଇଲେ ମହାଦେବଙ୍କ ବାପା ମଧ୍ୟ ଜାଣି ପରିବେ ନାହିଁ
objects.literal_meaning: If someone drinks water while submerged, even Mahadev’s father will not know.
objects.explanation: The dictionary places this example under doing something secretly. Drinking is hidden within the larger act of being underwater, so an observer cannot easily separate one from the other. The extravagant appeal to Mahadev’s father makes the claim of secrecy comic. It can describe someone’s confidence that a concealed action will escape notice; it does not establish that deception always succeeds.
objects.meaning_odia: ପାଣି ଭିତରେ ବୁଡ଼ିଥିବା ଲୋକ ପାଣି ପିଇଲେ, ବାହାରୁ ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ସେ କାମଟି ଅଲଗା କରି ଜଣାପଡ଼େ ନାହିଁ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାକୁ ଗୋପନରେ କାମ କରିବାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଭାବେ ଦେଇଛି। ମହାଦେବଙ୍କ ବାପା ବି ଜାଣିପାରିବେ ନାହିଁ କହି କଥାଟି ଲୁଚାଇବାର ଦାବିକୁ ହସରେ ବଢ଼ାଇଦିଏ। ଏଥିରୁ ସବୁ ଲୁଚା କାମ ଚିରକାଳ ଅଜଣା ରହିବ ବୋଲି ନିଶ୍ଚୟ କରିହୁଏ ନାହିଁ।
objects.english_summary: The dictionary places this example under doing something secretly.
objects.odia_summary: ପାଣି ଭିତରେ ବୁଡ଼ିଥିବା ଲୋକ ପାଣି ପିଇଲେ, ବାହାରୁ ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ସେ କାମଟି ଅଲଗା କରି ଜଣାପଡ଼େ ନାହିଁ।

objects.cultural_context: The expression is comic hyperbole, not theological genealogy or an instruction to drink underwater. Source spelling ପରିବେ is retained, not silently changed to ପାରିବେ.

objects.title: When a skill becomes a verdict
objects.literal_meaning: If, being a girl, she is not fit for kitchen work, her birth is wasted.
objects.explanation: The conditional turns a cooking expectation into a verdict on a girl’s entire life. The dictionary places this line under the act of cooking. Our critical reading questions that leap: a useful skill becomes a measure of human worth, imposed by gender. The source preserves the harsh judgment; it does not supply our rejection of it.
objects.meaning_odia: ରୋଷେଇର ଯୋଗ୍ୟତାକୁ ଏଠି ଝିଅର ସମଗ୍ର ଜୀବନର ରାୟ କରାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ପାକକର୍ମ ଅର୍ଥରେ ଏହି କଥା ଦିଏ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ସେହି ଡେଇଁବାକୁ ପଚାରେ: ଗୋଟିଏ ଦରକାରୀ କୌଶଳ କିପରି ଲିଙ୍ଗ ଆଧାରରେ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମାପେ? କଠୋର ରାୟଟି ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଛି; ତାହାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଆମର ପଢ଼ା।
objects.english_summary: Our critical reading questions measuring a girl’s worth by cooking ability.
objects.odia_summary: ରୋଷେଇରେ ଝିଅର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମାପିବାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।
objects.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a discussion of household expectations, a reader quotes the line. Another replies that everyone can learn useful kitchen skills, while nobody’s life becomes worthless for lacking one. They discuss sharing the work instead of testing only daughters. This is an invented critical conversation, not evidence of a traditional reply.
objects.cultural_context: Two related quotations occur in this one headword. They document gendered language, not the beliefs of every family or a named community. No origin date or endorsement is supplied.

objects.title: An invitation to make trouble
objects.literal_meaning: If you have no quarrel, take two wives; if the rice does not run out, keep two residences.
objects.explanation: The paired invitations offer ways to acquire trouble or use up provisions. Our reading hears irony rather than practical instruction. It also questions the first half’s gendered assumption: conflict is assigned to a marriage arrangement without hearing the people involved. The second half turns to the cost of maintaining two places. Neither household outcome is demonstrated by the saying.
objects.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ଝଗଡ଼ା ଆଣିବା ବା ଖାଦ୍ୟ ସରାଇବାର ଉପାୟ ରଖେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ, ବ୍ୟବହାରିକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଖଣ୍ଡର ଲିଙ୍ଗଭିତ୍ତିକ ଧାରଣାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆମେ ପଚାରୁଛୁ—ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତ ଲୋକଙ୍କ କଥା ନ ଶୁଣି ବିବାହର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାରେ ଝଗଡ଼ା ଧରାଯାଉଛି। ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଖଣ୍ଡ ଦୁଇ ସ୍ଥାନ ଚଳାଇବାର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚକୁ ଆଣେ। କୌଣସି ପରିବାରର ଫଳାଫଳ ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
objects.english_summary: Our reading hears ironic invitations to trouble while questioning the gendered premise.
objects.odia_summary: ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗାତ୍ମକ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ସହ ଲିଙ୍ଗଭିତ୍ତିକ ଧାରଣା ପ୍ରତି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
objects.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion of exaggerated advice, a reader quotes the paired invitations. Another notes the extra work of maintaining two places, then asks why the marriage half treats quarrelling as inevitable. This is an invented critical conversation, not household or legal advice.
objects.cultural_context: The source defines two residences. Its marriage language is historical evidence, not a recommendation, claim about women’s nature or account of present law or universal custom.

objects.title: Fruit and the mind
objects.literal_meaning: Fruit grows according to the mind.
objects.explanation: The entry explains the opening as according to one’s mental state or thought. Fruit supplies an image of an outcome. Our reading asks how an attitude shapes the way someone approaches work; it does not claim that thoughts alone control events. Neither success nor suffering can be diagnosed from this short line.
objects.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ନିଜ ମନ ବା ଚିନ୍ତା ଅନୁସାରେ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଫଳ ଏଠି ପରିଣାମର ଛବି ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ କାମକୁ କିପରି ଆଗେଇ ନିଏ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି; କେବଳ ଚିନ୍ତାରେ ଘଟଣା ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରିତ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଦାବି ନାହିଁ। ଏତିକି କଥାରୁ କାହାର ସଫଳତା ବା କଷ୍ଟର କାରଣ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
objects.english_summary: Our reading links outlook with approach, without promising control over results.
objects.odia_summary: ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ ଓ କାମର ଧାରାର ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ଫଳ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
objects.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରର କାମ ଆରମ୍ଭ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏଥିରେ କିଛି ହେବନି।” ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଫଳ କଣ ହେବ ଜାଣିନି; କିନ୍ତୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟାଟି ମନ ଦେଇ କରିବା।” / Before a reading-group project begins, someone dismisses it. A friend recalls the saying: “I cannot promise the outcome, but let us make a thoughtful attempt.” This exchange is invented.

objects.title: Onion and interest
objects.literal_meaning: Hindus do not eat onions; Pathans do not eat interest.
objects.explanation: The rhyme pairs eating onions with “eating” interest, giving two prohibitions the same verbal shape. The dictionary glosses biaja as loan interest and adds a religious explanation. Our critical reading notices how the line turns named communities into categorical statements. We retain those words as historical rhetoric, not as evidence of everyone’s diet, conduct or beliefs.
objects.meaning_odia: ପିଆଜ ଖାଇବା ସହ ସୁଧ “ଖାଇବା”କୁ ମେଳ ଦେଇ ଦୁଇ ନିଷେଧକୁ ଏକା ବାକ୍ୟଛାଞ୍ଚରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ବିଆଜର ଅର୍ଥ ଋଣର ସୁଧ ଦିଏ ଓ ଧାର୍ମିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ କିପରି ନାମିତ ସମୁଦାୟକୁ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଏକାଭଳି ଦାବିରେ ବଦଳାଯାଏ। ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦକୁ ଐତିହାସିକ କଥନ ଭାବେ ରଖୁଛୁ, ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ଖାଦ୍ୟ, ଆଚରଣ ବା ବିଶ୍ୱାସର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବେ ନୁହେଁ।
objects.english_summary: A rhyme makes categorical community claims that our reading questions.
objects.odia_summary: ଛନ୍ଦରେ ଗଢ଼ା ସମୁଦାୟର ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ଦାବିକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
objects.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ପିଆଜ ଓ ବିଆଜର ମେଳ ମନେ ରହେ; ତେଣୁ କଥାଟି ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏ କି?” ଆଲୋଚନାଟି ଶବ୍ଦର ମେଳ ଓ ଦାବିର ପ୍ରମାଣ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ତଫାତ ନେଇ ଚାଲିଲା। / A reading-group member asks, “The rhyme is memorable; does that make its claim true for everyone?” The group discusses the difference between verbal neatness and evidence. This exchange is invented.
objects.cultural_context: Pathan is the quotation’s term; the following note speaks more broadly of Muslims. That shift is not silently treated as identity equivalence. No present religious ruling or financial guidance is offered.

objects.title: Teaching the practised thief
objects.literal_meaning: Teaching an old hand at theft how to steal!
objects.explanation: The dictionary places this exclamation under a thief practised in the activity, separately from an elderly thief. Its joke makes the lesson unnecessary because the learner already knows the craft. Our everyday application questions instruction offered without first finding out what someone knows; it neither praises theft nor says experienced people cannot learn.
objects.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ଏହି ଅର୍ଥରେ ଚୋରଟି ଚୋରିରେ ପାରଙ୍ଗମ; କେବଳ ବୟସରେ ବୁଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ। ଯିଏ କାମଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣେ, ତାକୁ ସେହି କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାରେ କଥାର ମଜା। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଶିଖାଇବା ଆଗରୁ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କେତେ ଜାଣନ୍ତି, ତାହା ବୁଝିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହା ଚୋରିର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ବା ଅଭିଜ୍ଞ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଉ ଶିଖିବାର ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
objects.english_summary: An unnecessary lesson becomes the joke; our application asks about prior experience.
objects.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିଥିବା କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ନେଇ ମଜା; ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ପୂର୍ବ ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ଜାଣିବା ଜରୁରୀ।
objects.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସହକର୍ମୀ ଫାଇଲ ସଜାଇବା ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲେ। ରୀତା କହିଲେ, “ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିଟା ମୁଁ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲି; ତୁମ ପାଖରେ କିଛି ନୂଆ ଉପାୟ ଅଛି କି?” / A colleague begins explaining a filing method to its creator, who remains open to improvements. This scene is invented.
objects.cultural_context: The saying accompanies sense1, proficiency through practice. Sense2 separately describes an elderly thief. Neither establishes a real offender or an age-group trait.
